items.summary: The Canucks were following their first win in 11 games with their best game of the season. Then, suddenly, they weren’t.
items.body: The Vancouver Canucks were following their first win in 11 games with their best game of the National Hockey League season. Then, suddenly, they weren’t. Until Jonathan Lekkerimaki followed a risky neutral-zone turnover with his second interference penalty of the game at 6:59 of the third period, the Canucks looked almost comfortable carrying a two-goal lead over the San Jose Sharks. But Will Smith’s power-play goal sparked a three-goal outburst in just over three minutes as the Sharks exploded to beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 in San Jose. The Canucks pushed for a late tying goal, generating a couple of outstanding scoring chances while skating six-on-four and six-on-five, but were unable to salvage anything in the standings from a game in which they looked for 47 minutes as composed and structured as they have been this season. The loss followed Vancouver’s improbable 6-5 overtime road win Tuesday against the Anaheim Ducks. The Canucks were far sounder against Macklin Celebrini’s team in San Jose, plugging passing lanes, backchecking consistently and generally keeping the speedy Sharks in front of them after a couple of glaring breakdowns in the opening five minutes. Analytics site Natural Stat Trick had the Canucks better by a goal at five-on-five, and ahead 7-4 on high-danger scoring chances. But for the second time in just two tries (over 15 games), Vancouver failed to hold a lead they earned through 40 minutes. items.body: LOS ANGELES — Quinton Byfield scored at 3:37 of overtime and the Los Angeles Kings beat the Ottawa Senators 6-5 on Thursday night after blowing a four-goal lead in the third period. Byfield beat goalie Samuel Ersson with a snap shot from the high slot, with Drew Doughty picking up his third assist of the night on the play. Erik Haula tied it for Los Angeles on a first-period power play and Trevor Moore, Mikey Anderson, Joel Armia and Artemi Panarin scored in the second to make it 5-1. Panarin capped the run on a power play after Ottawa's Hayden Hodgson was tossed for boarding defenseman Brandt Clarke. Clarke missed the rest of the game because of an upper-body injury. Ottawa roared back in the third, with Shane Pinto tying it at 5 with 1:40 left and Ersson off for an extra attacker. Dylan Cozens scored twice in the period and Drake Batherson also connected. Cozens and Batherson struck in a 33-second span, and Cozens cut it to a goal with 7:26 remaining. Tyler Kleven opened the scoring for Ottawa in the first period. Jonas Johansson stopped 12 of 16 shots before giving way to Ersson in the second. Ersson made 20 saves on 22 shots.

items.title: ‘It meant a little more’: Seider on Red Wings’ win after Larkin suspension
items.summary: Larkin was suspended by the Red Wings on Thursday after he announced he would sit out until he was traded.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images Moritz Seider didn’t shy away from the importance of the Detroit Red Wings’ 4-1 win against the Chicago Blackhawks Thursday night, just hours after the franchise suspended former captain Dylan Larkin without pay . “It meant a little more,” Seider, who finished the night with an assist and 18:49 of ice time, told reporters after the game. “I think it came down to that this is our squad and we got a really good group in here.” The Red Wings suspended Larkin on Thursday after he announced through his agent he would no longer play for the team and sit out until he was traded. “It’s tough, but in the end, you just want him to be happy. If that’s not here, hopefully it’s somewhere else,” Seider said. “It’s kind of hard to put that player aspect aside and just see it as a friend, but ultimately, that’s my goal: him being happy and us being competitive.” The 25-year-old defenseman said he had no indication that Larkin was no longer willing to play for the team he captained for nearly six years. “We welcomed him with open arms, we were open-minded and didn’t let a situation like in Winnipeg happen,” a reference to Connor Hellebuyck’s trade request from the Winnipeg Jets that ended with him being traded to the New Jersey Devils earlier this week. “I think that’s a big credit to this locker room, too,” he added. “Now you just want to move on, figure some things out, and now some other guys will step up.” Seider also said he was hopeful the Red Wings get a good return in a potential Larkin trade. “You want this to be a proud organization where players want to be here, and want to be here long term. Hopefully, we can set a great example during the course of the year.”

items.summary: Will Smith scored twice, including the tying goal just 11 seconds before Mason Marchment’s go-ahead goal, and the San Jose Sharks rallied from a two-goal deficit to beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Thursday night.
items.body: SAN JOSE, Calif. — Will Smith scored twice, including the tying goal just 11 seconds before Mason Marchment’s go-ahead goal, and the San Jose Sharks rallied from a two-goal deficit to beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Thursday night. Marchment had a goal and an assist, while Macklin Celebrini recorded his 16th point of the season with an assist. Yaroslav Askarov made 23 saves for San Jose. Smith scored his first goal at 8:00 of the third period on a power play to get the Sharks on the board. San Jose had gone 0 for 4 on the power play before Smith’s goal. Smith tied the game with his second goal at 10:39, with Celebrini recording the assist. Marchment then gave the Sharks their first lead at 10:50. Drew O’Connor and Liam Ohgren scored for Vancouver, while Elias Pettersson and Filip Hronek had an assist. Leevi Merilainen stopped 21 shots for the Canucks. O’Connor opened the scoring at 13:21 of the first period for his second goal of the season, scoring on a rebound with an assist from Pettersson. San Jose defenseman Dmitry Orlov tried to clear the puck but was stripped, leading to the goal. Ohgren extended Vancouver’s lead to 2-0 at 18:56 of the second period with his fourth goal of the season. The Canucks have lost 11 of their last 12 games, having snapped a 10-game losing streak with their previous win. Sharks fans booed as Vancouver took its two-goal lead into the second intermission.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images The Ottawa Senators may have just lost another forward. Senators winger Andre Burakovsky left Thursday’s game against the Los Angeles Kings with an upper-body injury, and the team announced that he will not return to the game. The injury appeared to occur in the first period during a corner battle with Kings defenseman Mikey Anderson. Burakovsky fell to the ice after protecting the puck along the boards for an extended period of time, and was slow to get up. Ottawa is already missing forwards William Eklund and Warren Foegele due to injury. Burakovsky, 31, was scoreless in seven games coming into Thursday. The Austrian national missed four games earlier this season with an upper-body injury. It’s unclear if Thursday’s injury is at all related to his earlier injury. The Senators acquired Burakovsky from the Chicago Blackhawks this past offseason in exchange for a sixth-round pick in the 2027 NHL Entry Draft. Last season with Chicago, he notched 11 goals and 22 assists for 33 points in 75 games. Selected 23rd overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2013 NHL Draft, Burakovsky spent his first five NHL seasons in Washington before getting traded to the Colorado Avalanche in June of 2019 in exchange for forward Scott Kosmachuk and a third-round pick. He enjoyed his most productive years in Colorado, including the 2021-22 season in which he registered 22 goals and 39 assists for a career-high 61 points in 80 games. Burakovsky signed a five-year, $27.5 million contract as an unrestricted free agent with the Seattle Kraken in July of 2022. Hodgson has primarily served as an enforcer across his time with the AHL’s Lehigh Valley Phantoms, Ontario Reign, and Belleville Senators. items.summary: No Nick Suzuki, no Ivan Demidov, no Mike Matheson, no functional power play, no problem for the Canadiens. Eric Engels breaks down a collective game from Montreal to complete a perfect road trip.
items.body: No Nick Suzuki , no Ivan Demidov , no Mike Matheson , no functional power play, no problem for the Montreal Canadiens . But the collective game was there throughout the rest of this 4-0-0 road trip, with several different players stepping up to fill the massive void left by Suzuki. The Canadiens already had one big hole to patch, deprived of Demidov’s services since Game 3 of their season. But they at least got Matheson back for that first game against the Blackhawks after he missed four with a lower-body injury. items.body: Swedish journalist will be first from outside North America to receive Elmer Ferguson Memorial Award Born and raised in the hockey hotbed of Ornsköldsvik, hockey came naturally for Gunnar Nordstrom. The 73-year-old hockey reporter and columnist for Swedish daily Expressen is this year's recipient of the Elmer Ferguson Memorial Award, earning him induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame. He'll be the award's 67th recipient and the first from outside North America. "I knew my name had been mentioned in connection with the award, but I never thought I stood a chance of actually winning it," he said. "Occasionally, past recipients I guess just to be kind would say that, 'Well, you really deserve to win this award,' but I'd always reply, 'No, that will never happen.' But now it has, and it feels truly significant and a great honor. "Last year (chair of the selection committee) Eric Duhatschek let me know that I was one of six or seven candidates for this year's award, and that some felt it was time for an international journalist to be recognized. I mean, players from any country can be inducted, so why shouldn't a journalist be eligible too? Then, this summer, he called to tell me I'd won. At first, I thought it was a joke." The award, voted on by members of the Professional Hockey Writers Association, is presented, "in recognition of distinguished members of the hockey-writing profession whose words have brought honor to journalism and to hockey." It will be presented at the Hockey Hall of Fame's NHL Media Awards Luncheon in Toronto on Nov. 9. The goggles do come with one risk: A good chance you're getting teased if teammates see the Trac Optics goggles, which are designed to block out peripheral and lower vision, while sitting under the mask. "Get chirped all the time," said Dylan Garand of the New York Rangers. "Yeah, lots of 'Batman,'" Calgary Flames goalie Devin Cooley said with a laugh. Boston Bruins goalie Michael DiPietro 's wife also calls him Batman when he wears them around the house as the googles can be worn on or off the ice. Players at DiPietro's off-season skates were a little more pointed. "My shooters are like, 'What the hell are you wearing?'" DiPietro said. "I'm like, 'Guys, trust me, it makes my life way harder but (when) I take these off, I can actually see the puck way better.' It's funny, when you're looking at somebody wearing them, you're like, 'Are you serious, man? Are we complicating goaltending even more?' But it really is good for making sure you're actually moving your head, looking at pucks and tracking pucks." DiPietro primarily uses them in the offseason, preferring to focus on his signature battle-and-compete style during the season, though he has been using them a little more off the ice recently. "You don't really notice how much you use your peripheral vision until you have those things on, and it actually forces you to move your head," DiPietro said. items.title: Seider reacts to Larkin leaving Red Wings: ‘Turn the page’
items.summary: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade.
items.body: Moritz Seider is looking ahead as his former captain waits at home for a trade. The Detroit Red Wings ' top defenceman said, "It's good to put it in the past and turn the page," after Dylan Larkin left the team and was suspended without pay on Thursday. "Whoever we get, whatever pick we get, we'll have players that are happy to be here," Seider said after the Red Wings beat the Chicago Blackhawks 4-1. "We just have to make sure we get them ready to be part of our team." Larkin requested a trade out of Detroit in the spring but had been playing while awaiting a deal, even scoring a big goal late in a win over the Oilers on Monday. But on Thursday, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff announced that Larkin "has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings," so the team suspended the veteran centre as they weigh offers. The news came hours before the Red Wings hosted former teammate Patrick Kane and the rival Chicago Blackhawks in a game broadcast on ESPN, but after a slow start, Detroit rallied to win thanks to a hat trick from newcomer Viktor Arvidsson to improve to 6-4-3 on the season. "Obviously it meant a little more," Seider said of winning after the drama of the day. "I think it came down to this is our squad and we have a really good group in here." Seider, who is likely to succeed Larkin as captain, said he wishes nothing but the best to his now-former teammate. "Obviously it's tough but in the end you want him to be happy and if that's not here hopefully it's somewhere else," Seider said. "It's kinda hard to put that player aspect aside and just see it as a friend, but ultimately that's my goal... Nevertheless, we still have a hell of a group in here."

items.body: Register Login Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall Out Day-To-Day By Gabriel Foley | at October 29, 2026 7:10 pm Taylor Hall has fallen back out of the Carolina Hurricanes lineup with a day-to-day injury. The 34 year old sustained a new injury in Tuesday’s practice, unrelated to his upper-body injury sustained on October 13th, per ESPN’s Emily Kaplan . Hall has not played since his initial injury, though he was activated off of injured reserve on Monday . He went on to miss Tuesday’s game against the Boston Bruins, marking six consecutive absences for Hall. The Hurricanes offense is inevitably shorthanded without Hall in the lineup. His absence keeps Carolina from rolling out the trio of Hall, Logan Stankoven , and Jackson Blake – a unit that has outscored opponents 38-to-26 dating back to last season. They won the scoring battle three-to-one through the first eight games of this season. Individually, Hall has racked up five points in eight appearances. Half of that scoring came from back-to-back two-point performances on October 6th and 8th. The Hurricanes combined for 13 goals between those two games. Carolina has continued to find success despite Hall’s absence. They lead the NHL with a 10-2-2 record and rank third in scoring with 3.79 goals-per-game. Stankoven and Blake have been joined by Nikolaj Ehlers , forming a line that has four goals-for and no goals-against. Hall’s absence has also opened an opportunity for Nicolas Deslauriers , who should stick on the fourth-line until the former Hart Trophy winner is back to full health. items.summary: The PWHL is increasing the minimum pay for players, while also taking away the “reserve player” status from team roster builds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The PWHL is increasing the minimum player salary from around $38,000 to $42,000 for the 2026-27 season and will raise it to $52,500 by the 2030-31 season, the league and the PWHL Players Association announced Thursday. The increased salaries headline a list of sweeping changes to pay and roster construction, including teams increasing to 24-player rosters for the upcoming campaign and abolishing the league’s “reserve player” status, which had players in full-commitment but only making $15,000 as a full-season stipend. “As the PWHL expands from eight to 12 teams, these changes reflect our shared commitment to creating more opportunities for players, strengthening the economic foundation of professional women’s hockey and supporting the league’s long-term growth,” the joint statement said. “The PWHL and PWHLPA remain committed to working collaboratively to advance player opportunities, compensation, and the continued growth of professional women’s hockey.” With the increase in roster sizes, 288 players will be under contract for the 2026-27 season across the league’s dozen teams, now split into two conferences of six for the first time. At the same time, teams can use a One-Game Standard Player Agreement mechanism to sign replacements in case of injuries or other hardships that hit the roster. With the salary cap rising at a steep rate, promising individual performances can have even more weight as teams look to identify and pay players before those players can realize the full extent of their value on the open market. The Anaheim Ducks’ decision to pay Tristan Luneau , with less than 30 NHL games to his name, a $7.2MM AAV on a long-term contract extension serves as an illustration of this principle in action. One player who is lining himself up to earn a substantial pay raise is Minnesota Wild winger Max Shabanov . The 26-year-old former KHL star endured a difficult NHL rookie season with the New York Islanders in 2025-26, and New York ultimately non-tendered him after he scored just 18 points in 44 games. The Wild inked Shabanov to a one-year, $1.6MM deal, and he’ll be an RFA with arbitration rights over the summer. His early-season form suggests a major pay raise could be in store, as he’s found himself a regular role on Minnesota’s top power play unit and has produced nine points in his first 13 games with the Wild.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images The Buffalo Sabres have been here before. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images An experienced blueliner is headed across the border to the State of Hockey. On Thursday, the Minnesota Wild claimed defenseman Cameron Crotty off waivers from the Ottawa Senators . Crotty was put on waivers by the Senators on Wednesday after a rather uneventful start to the 2026-27 season. He played in just three of the team’s first 13 games, last getting into the lineup on Oct. 15, when Ottawa beat the New York Islanders in a shootout. The Ottawa native entered the year after appearing in six games with the Sens last season, his most NHL appearances in a single season. Crotty registered his first big-league point, an assist, on April 7 against the Tampa Bay Lightning . He even dressed for Ottawa in the postseason, playing in Game 3 of the team’s first-round series against the Carolina Hurricanes . Crotty spent the majority of the 2025-26 campaign with the Sens’ American Hockey League affiliate, the Belleville Senators, scoring three goals and 10 points in 49 games. This will be Crotty’s second stint with the Wild. He signed a one-year contract with the team as a free agent in July 2024, but only appeared in one game with Minnesota. items.title: Larkin decides to sit out until Red Wings complete trade
items.body: According to multiple sources, the Detroit Red Wings were informed Wednesday night that Dylan Larkin made the decision to sit out until he is traded. Those same sources indicated Larkin felt he had done right by them playing through his trade request, but “had enough” and it is time for the move to happen. Head coach Todd McLellan said Thursday morning Larkin wouldn’t play Thursday night against Chicago, and that interim GM Shawn Horcoff would address the situation. The Red Wings are expected to release a statement sometime Thursday. Sources indicate that Larkin’s agent, Pat Brisson, flew to Detroit this week to meet with Larkin face-to-face after the team’s recent road trip. That’s when the decision was made to take this step.

items.body: Artem Duda 's journey from U Sports to the NHL will be completed on Thursday night. The former Toronto Metropolitan University defenceman will make his NHL debut with the Utah Mammoth against the Pittsburgh Penguins, the team said after Thursday morning skate. A second-round pick of the Arizona Coyotes in 2022 (36th overall), the Russian-born Duda played the second half of the 2023-24 season with TMU after his appeal to play NCAA hockey at Maine was denied. Duda played 14 KHL games before going to TMU, where he played for the host team in the U Sports national championship. In 12 games with the Bold, Duda scored two goals and seven points. TMU lost in the Ontario final and then finished fourth at nationals on home ice. The 20-year-old joins the small contingent of U Sports athletes to play for an NHL organization, which includes the Stanley Cup-winning Logan Thompson. Duda has been with AHL Tucson since leaving TMU. He has one goal and two assists in six AHL games this season.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reported Thursday that winger Arthur Kaliyev has signed a 25-game professional tryout deal with the Iowa Wild, the top-level American Hockey League affiliate of the Minnesota Wild . items.title: Dylan Larkin to stay out of games until Red Wings complete trade
items.body: The Detroit Red Wings ' former captain will not play until a trade occurs, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Thursday. The development follows head coach Todd McLellan's announcement that Larkin will not play against the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. McLellan said Detroit's interim general manager Shawn Horcoff would address the situation. Larkin, 30, requested a trade during the summer. He did report to the team, but was stripped of his captaincy. The three-time all-star, who has a no-trade clause, has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press has reported that Larkin's list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations once he was removed from his post on July 15. That search is ongoing but Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. However, Red Wings assistant GM Kris Draper has watched the Canadiens live several times this season.

Veteran and franchise legend defenseman Victor Hedman will be back on the ice for the Bolts as they take on the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. Winger Brandon Hagel, who has not missed a game but had his status for this contest up in the air, will also play. Moser, Ryan McDonagh, John Carlson and Erik Cernak in the fold, the Lightning have been able to shelter Hedman and effectively manage his role in his age-35 season. Veteran forward Zemgus Girgensons will not play and is out on a day-to-day basis, and Tampa has plenty of depth defensively to spread minutes around on the back end. The Lightning, perennially one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, have looked like such to start this season, but a dearth of games played compared to their Atlantic Division foes has them sitting in sixth in the division by points, though they’re second by points percentage. Despite the overall strong start, Tampa has dropped its past two games as the Jets come to town, so the Bolts will be looking to get right against a Winnipeg team that started the year out hot but has lost six straight games to plummet down the Central Division standings.

items.body: Mike Babcock has made no bones about his desire for the Edmonton Oilers to become tougher to play against. He isn’t seeking just a mindset approach, either. Babcock has campaigned internally for more size and brawn in his forward group, which GM Stan Bowman is now examining on the trade market. One name that Babcock is believed to admire is New York Rangers forward Matt Rempe . Would the cost for Rempe be a mid-round pick? He figures to be available – because both Peter Laviolette and now Mike Sullivan haven’t exactly figured out the best way to utilize him other than spot duty. The 6-foot-9 Rempire State Building is four seasons into his NHL career and has cracked the lineup for a total of 87 career games, including just two this season. Rempe, 24, has averaged 6:46 in ice time over those two contests. Rempe is a legit heavyweight in any era at 270 pounds and in today’s NHL, a more than willing combatant with 11 career bouts on his fight card. It’s not necessarily that the Oilers need a fighter, but perhaps a deterrent so opponents are less inclined to take liberties with Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. Plus, so much of Edmonton’s bottom half of their forward corps is homogenous or similar. They could use a change of pace. Rempe is a Calgary native who began his junior career with the Spruce Grove Saints just outside of Edmonton. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Pittsburgh Penguins forward Ben Kindel is set to return to game action on Thursday against the the Utah Mammoth less than a week after suffering a medical episode on a team flight. items.title: Injured Panthers Brad Marchand, Aleksander Barkov resume skating
items.summary: The Florida Panthers could be about a month away from nearing full forward health.
items.body: The Florida Panthers could be about a month away from nearing full forward health. Captain Aleksander Barkov and veteran winger Brad Marchand both resumed skating Thursday as they take a step toward a return from injury, head coach Paul Maurice told reporters . Barkov remains four weeks away from playing games while Marchand is three weeks out, Maurice added. The captain, who missed all of last season due to a right knee injury, went down in just his second game this season with a left knee injury that ultimately did not require surgery. His original timeline of six to eight weeks from the early October exit appears to still be intact. Marchand has also been out since early October with a left leg injury. “We’re no stranger to guys going down the last few years, and guys have done a great job of stepping up," Matthew Tkachuk said in the wake of the Marchand injury. “Worst case, you just got to win 1-0, 2-1.” Indeed, the Panthers have held their own without the star forwards, going 7-4-2 record in 13 games to hold the top wild-card spot in the East.

Shesterkin’s injury, along with a more minor injury suffered by veteran backup Joonas Korpisalo , has allowed goalie prospect Dylan Garand to have his longest stint in the NHL of his young career. So far, he’s generally impressed, even if he’s slowed down a bit as of late. Garand’s emergence could pay dividends for a Rangers team that traded away significant draft capital over the summer. According to The Athletic’s Vince Z. Mercogliano , the Rangers may try to capitalize on Garand’s increasing value next summer by trading him away, assuming Garand “puts together a solid season and teams come calling about a trade.” Mercogliano pointed out that New York’s situation with Garand is not entirely dissimilar to the situation they found themselves in back in 2015, when Cam Talbot emerged as a future No. 1 goalie while he was still Henrik Lundqvist’s backup. Some Power Players even get to travel to different marquee events throughout the season. Xu described hockey as a “consistent presence in my life,” and said she’s been watching the sport with her dad over the last few years. “That’s something that brings me a lot of comfort and something I greatly value,” she said. items.body: Tristan Jarry made 24 stops to earn the shutout as the Edmonton Oilers snapped a two-game losing skid, defeating the rival Calgary Flames 4-0 on Wednesday. Mathieu Joseph, Mattias Ekholm, Kasperi Kapanen and Alex Formenton had the goals for the Oilers (9-2-2). Connor McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins each had a pair of assists. Edmonton wrapped up its five-game road trip with a 3-1-1 record. The Flames (5-7-0) saw a four-game winning streak come to an end. Dustin Wolf recorded 20 saves for Calgary, coming in to replace Devin Cooley (eight saves) who was injured late in the first period. Flames: Cooley was run over in the crease by Oilers forward Colton Dach late in the first and did not return to start the second. The 29-year-old has been on fire of late, coming into the contest with four straight wins, during which he had a 1.50 goals-against average and .955 save percentage. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points streak to all 13 games, adding two assists to give him a league-leading 36 points. He also extended his campaign-starting assists streak to 13 games, setting a new record by surpassing the likes of Sebastian Aho, Ken Linseman and Wayne Gretzky for the longest in NHL history. Edmonton made it 3-0 on the power play just 55 seconds into the third with a nice display of passing as McDavid sent it to Kapanen for his fourth. The Oilers are now 7-0-1 when scoring first and 7-0 when leading after 40 minutes. By contrast, Calgary is 1-6 when allowing the first goal and 0-5 when behind after the second. With that date approaching, he has formally signed through the end of the 2026-27 season. Shore is among Lugano’s top scorers, with 13 points in 14 league games with the club. A full-season contract will commit Shore to a full season in Switzerland’s top league, a setting he has already thrived in before. Shore won a National League championship with EV Zug in 2021. He scored 27 points in 22 games, then added eight points in 13 playoff matchups. That was his first season overseas, though he began the year in Slovakia’s top league with HK Dukla Trencin. Switzerland, and a championship, must have made a warm impression, as Shore went on to join HC Ambri-Piotta for the start of the 2022-23 season. He made another mid-season move that year, heading to HV71 in Sweden’s SHL. Shore stayed in the SHL – splitting his time between HV71 and Linkoping HC – until the end of the 2025-26 season. He totaled 99 points in 157 games in what is largely considered one of the top-five pro leagues in the world. Just a few months later, he returned to Switzerland to chase another Swiss title. Despite strong scoring at the top of their lineup – including scoring leader Jere Innala ’s point-per-game pace – Lugano has struggled to start the year. What's gone wrong and what needs to change? For much, if not most of his final season as an Edmonton Oilers defenseman, Darnell Nurse was a flashpoint of controversy. While Nurse wasn't the 1A blueliner his $9.25-million annual salary would suggest, he became a focal point of fan and management frustration largely because of the cap hit that was attached to him. Now that he's gone, another Oilers D-man is in the early stages of replacing Nurse as a target for frustration: Jake Walman. More Videos Edmonton coach Mike Babcock's recent usage of Walman — and the fact he was made a healthy scratch for the Oilers Wednesday game against the Calgary Flames — suggests he could become a whipping boy sooner than later. Some of that is unfair, at least, at this stage in Walman's season. He's played only nine games, posting just one point in that span. But he was never signed to his lucrative extension to be a major point-producer. Walman's best offensive season came in 2024-25, when he posted 40 points in 65 games between the San Jose Sharks and the Oilers. He hasn't reached that level of scoring since, but the bigger problem area right now is Walman's minus-7 rating. Plus-minus isn't a perfect indicator of a player's effectiveness, but it's one of many factors indicating Walman's defensive struggles. Most feature clichés about getting pucks deep, playing a full 60 minutes, and taking things one game at a time. Honesty and bluntness? More like: let’s avoid headlines and not be bigger than the team. Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley is changing all of that, though, and has taken a different approach. In recent weeks, Cooley, seemingly on a path towards personal enlightenment, has gone viral for his answers, swapping hockey clichés for philosophical musings on life, death, consciousness, and also goaltending. Cooley’s latest wave of insight began on October 18 during an interview with Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker. “I felt nothing,” Cooley said minutes after beating the Carolina Hurricanes 3-2. “The problem with me is that I have a lot of fun playing, but when I start having too much fun, it [changes me] from an unconscious goalie to a conscious goalie, and my conscious brain is really bad at playing goalie. “So I have to let my unconscious brain do the work, because it reacts a lot quicker…Like, don’t think about anything. items.body: Register Login Evening Notes: Dickinson, MacDonald, Jacobs By Gabriel Foley | at October 28, 2026 5:52 pm As expected, the Edmonton Oilers activated centerman Jason Dickinson off of injured reserve ahead of Wednesday’s clash against the rival Calgary Flames. Dickinson missed Edmonton’s last six games after sustaining a groin injury in the Oilers’ practice on October 14th. He returned to regular practices on Tuesday and should get a chance to ease into the lineup in Wednesday’s home matchup, before Edmonton embarks on a three-game road trip. Dickinson faced a nagging ankle injury to start the season. Between that injury and his recent groin injury, the 31 year old has been limited to just three games this season. He has one assist, three shot blocks, and three hits in those appearances. His return should bump rookie Owen Michaels to the fourth-line center role, while Colton Dach likely shifts to the press box. The Oilers will bring slightly more depth into an important stretch of matchups. They’ll look to maintain a hot streak – and better support superstars Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl – after posting a 7-2-1 record across their last 10 games.
